LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (2 sessions) • Reordering jumbled 
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing: Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Handwriting, part of Writing 3.1 Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (2 sessions) • Reordering jumbled  in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why is it good to write clearly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to identify features of good Arabic handwriting,

2. list the features on a chart for display,

3. work jointly to create a well-written story based on the theme,

4. share their write-ups for peer assessment,

5. team up to conduct a writing contest to hone their Arabic writing skills,

6. publish the best-written compositions in the school or public children’s magazine.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to identify features of good Arabic handwriting,
2. list the features on a chart for display,
3. work jointly to create a well-written story based on the theme,
4. share their write-ups for peer assessment,
5. team up to conduct a writing contest to hone their Arabic writing skills,
6. publish the best-written compositions in the school or public children’s magazine.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner embraces new ideas that inspire creativity when creating a

well-written story based on the theme.

• Learning to Learn: This is nurtured as the learner is motivated to learn continuously by conducting a writing contest to

hone their Arabic writing skills.
